impasse_procedure.value: Mediation by the Agency on a deadlock (no power of compulsion). Then by strike class: class 1 (police, fire, corrections, hospital) goes to binding arbitration; class 2 may strike for a limited time after mediation, with arbitration if the deadlock outlasts an injunction; class 3 may strike after a majority secret-ballot vote. School employees (municipal school districts, regional educational attendance areas, state boarding schools) must first submit to advisory arbitration before a strike vote; if it fails, a strike needs 72 hours' notice and may not begin on or after the first day of the school term until one day in session has passed after notice.
impasse_procedure.quote: If, after a reasonable period of negotiation over the terms of a collective bargaining agreement, a deadlock exists between a public employer and an organization, the labor relations agency may appoint a competent, impartial, disinterested person to act as mediator

strike_legality.value: Depends on class. Police, fire, corrections and hospital employees may not strike; class 2 (utility, snow removal, sanitation, some educational employees) may strike for a limited time after mediation; all others may strike after a majority secret-ballot vote. School employees (municipal school districts, regional educational attendance areas, state boarding schools) must first submit to advisory arbitration before a strike vote; if it fails, a strike needs 72 hours' notice and may not begin on or after the first day of the school term until one day in session has passed after notice.
strike_legality.quote: The class in (a)(1) of this section is composed of police and fire protection employees, jail, prison, and other correctional institution employees, and hospital employees. Employees in this class may not engage in strikes.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018). The statute's service-fee option, AS 23.40.110(b)(2), is still in the text.
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.
